text: Using MIT-licensed code inside a closed-source proprietary product.
Using an OpenRAIL-M model for a use listed in the licence's prohibited-uses appendix.
Shipping MPL-2.0 files inside a larger proprietary product while keeping the source of the MPL-covered files available.
Commercially fine-tuning and deploying an OpenRAIL model for a use that is NOT in its restricted-uses list.
Running modified AGPL-3.0 software for a single internal user with no other users interacting with it over a network.
Distributing a binary of GPL-3.0 software to customers while refusing to provide the corresponding source.
Commercially deploying Apache-2.0 code and relying on its express patent grant.
Redistributing Apache-2.0 code after deleting the required NOTICE file.
Incorporating Apache-2.0 code into a GPL-3.0-licensed project.
Dynamically linking an LGPL-2.1 library from proprietary software while allowing the user to replace the library.
Distributing a single binary that statically links a GPL-2.0-only library together with Apache-2.0 code.
Modifying GPL-3.0 software and running it only internally, with no distribution, and not releasing the source.
Any use, including commercial, of a work dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
Providing Elastic-License-2.0 software to third parties as a hosted, managed service.
Creating a modified version of a CC BY-ND 4.0 work and distributing that derivative.
Deploying a product built on Meta's Llama 3 Community License model with 800 million monthly active users, without a separate Meta licence.
Distributing a modified BSD-3-Clause library using the original author's name to endorse it.
Selling a support subscription for unmodified GPL-2.0 software you distribute with full source.
Combining GPL-3.0 and GPL-2.0-only code in one distributed binary.
Using an MIT library and only reproducing its licence text in an ABOUT screen.
Offering AGPL-3.0 software as a network service without offering the (modified) source to users.
Fine-tuning a CC-BY-4.0 dataset model and attributing the dataset in the model card.
Redistributing a CC-BY-SA-4.0 work under a more restrictive proprietary licence.
Statically linking an MPL-2.0 file into a proprietary binary, keeping the MPL files' source available.
Using an OpenRAIL-M model for a use explicitly in the licence's prohibited-uses appendix.
Deploying a Llama-3 model with under 700M MAU commercially.
Deploying a Llama-3 model at 800M MAU without a separate Meta licence.
Publishing benchmark results of a proprietary model whose terms forbid publishing comparisons.
Using a public-domain (CC0) work in a commercial closed product with no attribution.
Removing copyright headers from Apache-2.0 files before redistribution.
Dynamically linking an LGPL-3.0 library from proprietary code, allowing user relinking.
Hosting Elastic-License-2.0 software as a managed service for third parties.
